invariants: Seventeen actual Source/native observations cover canonical JSONL with compression none and zstd; no retired Source SQLite provider is mounted.

listSnapshots exposes detached headers and tokens qualified by dev/ino/size/mtimeNs/ctimeNs. The plaintext restored-stat fixture explicitly controls Windows ChangeTime on both sides; arbitrary rewrites preserving every stat field remain outside the guarantee.

Both compression modes cover lazy creation, repeated stable reads, nonempty append, no-op append, detached mutation, reopening, copying and exact caller pre-abort. The extra plaintext restored-stat row completes the seventeen observations.
Lazy creation produces no stored snapshot; no-op append preserves the token. Reopen preserves identity while a copied log has a different physical identity.
Pre-abort precedes backend work; asynchronous stat completion/error checks cancellation before publication or missing-log handling.
File-attribute handles close after success/failure; long Unicode Windows paths use Win7-compatible extended-path handling.
identity: Tokens identify a physical JSONL log revision; seventeen paired observations assert declared stable/change/copy semantics independently.
ownership: The JSONL provider owns file operations and temporary Win32 attribute handles; callers own cancellation reasons and detached returned headers.
ordering: Validate pre-abort, capture provider state, check cancellation at asynchronous stat boundaries, then publish detached snapshots.
errors: Preserve exact caller abort and native stat failures; omit missing logs only after checking cancellation.
cancellation: Pre-abort and JSONL stat-failure boundaries are tested. Full provider epoch/FTS reconciliation and shared-task close/abort serialization remain outside this contract.
adaptation: Python uses the canonical JSONL provider for both compression modes. Native Windows file identity/ChangeTime corresponds to the actual Source stat token; finite fixtures do not certify arbitrary cross-process or power-loss histories.
open_questions: All provider epochs, incremental FTS generations, two-attempt reconciliation, raw duplicate-artifact ordering and non-Windows physical birthtime qualification remain unaccepted.

rc1_review.scope: Current finite executable provider/consumer corpora, original-browser and extracted observations in the single full receipt. Historical alpha evidence remains historical; no inventory-wide parity, arbitrary ABI/history, paid-provider or Win7 certification.

historical_native_compatibility_notes: Legacy native SQLite unit controls retain store UUID, incarnation, transactional revision and atomic backfill coverage. They neither mount a canonical rc.1 SQLite persistence package nor add Source rows; the removed Source provider and its old acceptance remain in alpha history.
